meta.title: Indoor search rover — practical BOM
meta.intro: One list, everything on the rover, including what you already own. Owned rows are pre-ticked and cost $0. Every part has a position in millimetres and the fastener that holds it, computed in assembly.py from the frame geometry — not eyeballed. Prices observed September 4–5, 2026; stock and checkout prices can change. Physical validation is still outstanding.
meta.margin_note: Margin = torque available ÷ torque required; acceptance ≥ 1.25 because the running torque is calculated, not measured. Keep total mass under about 5.2 kg or the ramp margin is gone — that is why the power bank was dropped for a 5 V buck. The one measurement that matters most: pull-out torque at 24 rpm, 1.5 A, on the real battery.
meta.not_analysed: Fatigue, buckling, impact, vibration, roller wear, uneven floors and wheel unloading, combined-slip mecanum behaviour, motor and driver thermal equilibrium, battery sag under stall, firmware timing, fastener pull-out in PETG, deck deflection under the turret, servo torque with the camera fitted, motor-bearing radial rating (assumed 28 N — thinnest margin in the design), and radar detection at 300 mm height (Walleye measured floor-level radar as blind; this is a compromise to test). No physical test has been run.

design: Four independently driven 80 mm mecanum wheels on the four owned NEMA 17 steppers, a low 350 × 390 mm 2020 frame, the battery slung under the deck for a low centre of gravity, the Ceres pan/tilt turret at the front carrying the USB camera so it can look around and track, and both radars on a 200 mm post at the rear looking forward over the turret. Four short-range ToF sensors guard each side. The fifth motor and TB6600 stay spare.

No kit does this. Every mecanum chassis kit on Amazon is built for TT or DC gearmotors; none has a NEMA 17 mount. Steel L-brackets under the rails are the cleanest way to put your steppers on mecanum wheels, and the 5 mm couplers in the wheel set match the 5 mm flatted shaft on your motors.

Power is one LiPo. It feeds the motor drivers directly, a 5 V buck for the Pi, and the Ceres 6 V buck for the servos. The power bank is gone: 350 g of unknown mass was the difference between passing and failing the ramp case.

LD2410C is the primary presence sensor, including stationary/micro-moving presence. LD2450 adds positions and speeds of moving targets; it is not the primary detector for an immobile person. Neither outputs heartbeat measurements. Start with one radar powered; test the two radar types separately, then together for interference. These sensors are not validated here for finding a motionless person behind concrete, rubble, fire or smoke. No detection must never be interpreted as proof that nobody is present.
power: LiPo XT60 -> XT60 pigtail -> three 18 AWG branches: shield VMOT (four DRV8825 -> four motors), 5 V buck IN, 6 V buck IN. No fuse, by your call — the XT60 is the disconnect, so keep the pack leads short and sleeved.
5 V buck OUT -> Pi GPIO pins 2/4 (5 V) and 6 (GND). Set it to 5.10 V unloaded with the multimeter before the Pi is connected. Pi USB-A -> Uno USB-B for logic power and serial.
6 V buck OUT -> PCA9685 V+ terminal (Ceres). Set to 6.0 V before connecting. Servo current returns through the PCA9685 terminal, never through a USB ground.
Pi -> camera by USB. Pi -> ESP32-S3 by USB-C; the ESP32 bridges both radar UARTs. Radars take 5 V power and 3.3 V UART signalling.
Four VL53L1X share I2C only after XSHUT (GPIO 5, 6, 13, 19) assigns unique addresses at boot. PCA9685 is on the same I2C bus at 0x40.
Single common ground at the shield GND terminal. Never put LiPo voltage on a logic rail.
power_after: Motors at 1.5 A per phase draw about 2 A from the pack at cruise — copper loss dominates, not motion. The 5200 mAh pack runs motors for roughly two hours. Holding current at rest costs the same as moving, so cut ENABLE (D8) when parked; mecanum wheels on a level floor do not roll away.
The owned three-pin switch is not in the load path until its DC rating is read off the body and is at least 10 A.
fit: Frame: two side rails along X with outer faces at Y = ±195; two cross rails along Y butted between them with outer faces at X = ±175. Rails sit at Z 71–91. Eight corner brackets, one top and one bottom at each joint, M5 T-nuts, 3.0 N·m maximum or the slot deforms.

Drive: each steel L-bracket goes inverted under a side rail near its end, foot against the rail underside on two M4 T-nuts, leg hanging down flush with the rail's outer face. The motor bolts to the inboard side of the leg with four M3×6 at 0.8 N·m (aluminium threads — the full 1.1 N·m an M3 can take will strip the flange). Shaft through the leg, coupler on the flat with blue threadlocker, wheel on the coupler. Axle at X = ±125, Z = 40. Motor body bottom at Z = 18.9 mm: that is your ground clearance.

Mecanum handedness: front-left and rear-right take the left-hand wheels, front-right and rear-left the right-hand. Check from above — the rollers on top of each wheel should point toward the chassis centre, forming an X.

Deck: two PETG tiles 170 × 350 × 5 on the rail tops, six M5 T-nuts each. Battery cradle hangs under the deck centre on four M4×16 bolts — battery bottom at Z 64, well above the motors. Uno/shield stack rear-left, Pi rear-right, both bucks ahead of the Uno, PCA9685 beside the Pi, ESP32 rear-centre under the post. Turret base at X = +110 on the front tile. Radar post on the rear cross rail through the deck, radars at Z = 300 facing forward, 100 mm apart.
compute: Load cases at the design mass, 80 mm wheels, mecanum roller factor √2, mechanical efficiency 0.85, carpet rolling coefficient 0.12: level cruise, level at 0.3 m/s², strafing, and a 5° carpet ramp at 0.3 m/s². The ramp governs. Available torque is holding torque × (I / 1.7 A) × 0.70, where 0.70 is a conservative low-speed pull-out factor that has not been measured. Full arithmetic, every input tagged measured / allocated / assumed, is in drivetrain.txt; every placement is in assembly.csv.

At 1/8 microstepping, 0.1 m/s is about 637 pulses/s per wheel and 0.3 m/s about 1,910 — inside a 5,000/axis timer-interrupt budget on the Uno. Custom four-axis firmware with acceleration limits, shared enable and a communication timeout; GRBL is unsuitable. Motor order at the shield: X = FL, Y = FR, Z = RL, A = RR with the D12/D13 jumpers fitted.

Set DRV8825 current with Vref = 5 × Rsense × I. With 0.100 Ω sense resistors, 1.5 A is 0.75 V; read the actual resistor first. Start at 1.5 A with heatsinks and the fan; 1.7 A is the reserve, not the default.

Before calling it working: caliper every part marked VERIFY before drilling the deck; measure pull-out torque at 24 rpm and 1.5 A on the real battery with a lever arm and the hanging scale; then all four wheel directions raised; loaded forward, reverse, strafe, turn; watchdog stop; temperature after 10 minutes; radar trials one at a time then together; turret tracking with the camera fitted; marked-route obstacle stops. None of these tests has been performed.

items.note: Four drive wheels, fifth spare. 0.41 N·m holding, 1.7 A, 240 g each, 5 mm flatted shaft.

items.item: SmaringRobot 4× 80 mm mecanum wheels with 5 mm couplings
items.note: Two left-hand, two right-hand. Coupler fits the motor's 5 mm flatted shaft; do not print a hub.

items.item: Anndason 6× steel NEMA 17 L-brackets with screws
items.note: Four used, two spare. 3 mm steel, 113 g each. Base slots are 4.3 mm: M4 T-nuts, not M5.
All four used at full length. Nothing to cut.

items.item: TOCLUX 20× 2020 corner brackets with M5 screws and T-nuts
items.note: Eight for the frame corners; the rest and the 40 M5 T-nuts cover deck and post attachment.

items.item: Bemaka 2020 T-nut kit, M3/M4/M5, with M4×10 and M4×12 screws
items.note: The M4 T-nuts and M4×10 screws hold the motor brackets to the rails.
Two deck tiles, battery cradle, radar post + bar, fan bridge, four ToF clips. ~0.5 kg of the spool.

items.item: ELEGOO Uno R3 with USB cable
items.note: Generates the step pulses on a timer interrupt. The included USB cable runs to the Pi.

items.item: CNC Shield V3 kit with 4× DRV8825 drivers and heatsinks
items.note: Required, not optional: A4988 fails the ramp case. Fit the D12/D13 jumpers for the fourth axis. Vref = 5 × Rsense × I.
One over the drivers on a printed bridge, one spare. Powered from the 5 V buck.
Spare. No fifth axis in this design.

items.note: 343 g, 132 × 43 × 25 mm. Slung under the deck centre — the lowest heavy part on the rover.

items.item: DROK 8–35 V to 5 V 3 A buck converter
items.note: Replaces the power bank (−310 g). Feeds the Pi on GPIO 5 V. Set 5.10 V before connecting.
From the Ceres turret rail. Confirm it is still in the box; feeds PCA9685 V+.

items.item: SKYRC B6AC Neo balance charger, 60 W AC
items.note: Start at 2.6 A = 0.5 C. Follow the pack's instructions.

On the balance lead, velcroed to the cradle side.

Camera, radar processing, servo control, interface. Model still unknown — affects the 5 V budget.
